name: Casual chic

card.summary: A relaxed-but-polished way of dressing that pairs tailored pieces with casual ones so outfits look put-together without looking formal.
card.note: There is no official rulebook; interpretation varies by setting.

quick.overview:
Casual chic is a style approach that blends relaxed garments, such as jeans, T-shirts and clean sneakers, with polished, tailored ones like blazers, fine knits and leather loafers. The aim is an outfit that looks considered without looking stiff or overdressed.

Its appearance payoff comes from fit and refinement: the same casual pieces look sharper when cut well, in understated colours and clean finishes, which makes it a flexible way to look put-together for dinners, parties and informal workplaces.
quick.how: Style guides describe pairing one tailored item with a casual one: a blazer over a plain T-shirt with well-fitting dark jeans, an overshirt with chinos, or a fine sweater with smart trousers. Colours stay understated (navy, grey, beige), shoes are clean leather loafers or minimalist sneakers, and accessories are restrained, such as a simple watch and belt.
quick.risks: There is no real risk beyond misjudging a dress code. Because the term has no formal definition, the same outfit may read as too casual or too dressy depending on the venue.

lead: Casual chic is a style approach that combines relaxed clothing with polished, tailored pieces so an outfit looks put-together without seeming stiff or overdressed.[1] Retail style guides describe it as suitable for parties, dinners and informal business settings.[1]

People use it to look sharper while staying comfortable: tailored items such as blazers or smart trousers are mixed with jeans, T-shirts or sneakers, and fit and fabric do much of the work.[1][2] It sits close to "smart casual", an ambiguous Western dress code that Wikipedia traces to a 1924 newspaper usage, and to business casual.[2][3]
The term has no official definition, and the guidance comes mainly from fashion retailers and style writers rather than formal sources.

chain: Tailored pieces mixed with casual ones
Looks polished and put-together while relaxed
angle.text: Wearing a well-fitting blazer, overshirt or fine knit with dark jeans or chinos and clean shoes makes everyday outfits look more refined. It gives a wide range of occasions a single flexible look.

infobox: Blazer, overshirt, dark jeans, loafers, minimalist sneakers

paras: One retailer's guide frames casual chic as sitting between smart and relaxed, with the goal of looking put-together without being overdressed.[1] Typical garments it lists are blazers, overshirts, shirts, premium T-shirts, smart loafers, and polished jeans, chinos or tailored trousers.[1]

The same guide recommends slim or regular fit jeans in dark indigo or black without rips or heavy washing, understated colours such as navy, grey and beige, and no bold logos.[1] For footwear it suggests clean, minimalist, slim-soled leather sneakers or loafers, with accessories limited to items like a minimalist watch and leather belt.[1]

Smart casual is described on Wikipedia as an ambiguously defined dress code that combines casual wear with elements of a lounge suit; typical men's pieces include chinos, collared shirts and odd-coloured blazers.[2] Business casual is a form of smart casual worn in white-collar workplaces, associated with Casual Fridays that began in California in the 1990s, inspired by Hawaii's Aloha Friday.[3] Wikipedia notes that interpretation depends on context, location and personal judgement.[2]
